title: Head Position
shortDefinition: The head is a post, wedge, pressure source, and sensor that organizes the spine.
whyItMatters: Bad head position exposes guillotines, kills underhooks, invites shoulder crunch, or loses passing angle.
deepExplanation: Head position decides where shoulders and hips can move. Ear to ribs supports wrestle-up; offset head near hip supports bodylock pass; head beside opponent’s head retains back control.
beginnerView: Do not let the head float or sit between both opponent hands.
advancedView: Use the head to cut shoulder line or hip line before using hands.

ifThenExamples.if: If you lose Head Position during the exchange.
ifThenExamples.then: Stop accelerating, recover the nearest body structure, then continue the technique.
ifThenExamples.why: Modern no-gi punishes forceful continuation after structure is lost.

ifThenExamples.if: If the opponent correctly answers your first line.
ifThenExamples.then: Use Head Position to switch to a safer branch instead of forcing the same line.
ifThenExamples.why: A good concept turns the opponent’s reaction into information for the next decision.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Head Position is a single technical trick.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: Treat it as a decision rule that appears across many positions.

commonMisunderstandings.misunderstanding: Understanding the concept automatically makes it work live.
commonMisunderstandings.correction: The concept needs body signals, short cues, and positional rolling.

trainingCues: Name Head Position before adding force.
Find the body signal instead of guessing generally.
If structure is lost, reset one layer first.
Drill slowly, then test with progressive resistance.
